benchmarks.task_description:
fix(workspace): preserve actionable shell diagnostics in model results

When Bash reports a missing command, the model-facing Shell projection currently drops the Runner's diagnostic and its recovery advice. Preserve only diagnostic `code`, `command`, and `instruction` across synchronous results, managed completion, and execution management tools, while retaining the existing stream handling and credential exclusions.

Clarify that an unavailable managed Shell leaves the independent Python execution channel unaffected; `python -c` through `run_shell` still requires Bash. Extend native Windows command-shim coverage to both `.cmd` and `.bat`, literal metacharacters, and explicit rejection of unsupported characters.

Follow-up to #716; related to #916. The diagnostic projection regression was introduced after #716's original managed execution path.

## Validation

- Native Windows 11 x64 (10.0.26200), Node 22.23.4, local Runner, `none` execution mode.
- Diagnostic projection and Runner diagnostic tests: **8 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**. Before the product fix, all six affected projection entry points failed because the diagnostic was missing.
- Stack-platform/helper tests: **13 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**. Both shim extensions preserve spaces, `&`, and literal `%PATH%`; NUL, CR, LF, and quotes are explicitly rejected.
- Product build and test TypeScript check passed.
- Additional selected existing regressions: **12 executed, 11 passed, 1 environment failure**. The failure occurs while preparing a Windows symlink (`EPERM`), before Shell execution. These Linux-tagged tests were run from temporary copies with Windows added to the tags; assertions were unchanged. Initial platform-excluded runs are not counted as passes.
- Full local UT/ST/E2E suites were **not run**, per the task's explicit scope restriction. No full-suite pass is claimed.

Commands: `node --import tsx --test packages/workspace/src/shell-diagnostic-view.test.ts services/runner/src/shell-diagnostics.test.ts`, `node --test scripts/stack-platform.test.mjs`, `pnpm -r build`, and `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`.

## E2E user journeys

**PASS:** Six chat scenarios through the running product's HTTP API and a local scripted model: immediate missing-command diagnosis, background completion observed through `execution_status`, stdout false-positive rejection, successful guaranteed utilities, pre-dispatch Shell refusal with no execution record, and successful Shell execution after restoring Bash. All six Runs completed and the model-facing tool messages were inspected.

Additional real Runner/setup acceptance:

- A fresh starter provides the six guaranteed utilities. `sort` also works, recorded only as an additional observation.
- A genuine old starter was created through product setup at `b31f74eb368a0e07848c2aa72acf9451348471bb`, whose Windows package contract adds only `m2-bash`. The candidate requests only `m2-coreutils`, `m2-grep`, and `m2-sed`, creates an audit revision, and preserves the original revision.
- Restarting after upgrade leaves the catalog and all **16,847 installed file hashes unchanged**, with no extra revision.
- With only the isolated instance's Bash unavailable, Runner readiness remains true, independent Python HTTP execution succeeds, and accepted managed Shell submissions settle as deterministic `not_started` failures without a fabricated result or version.
- With a deliberately failing isolated channel and an empty package cache, upgrade fails while the Runner process/heartbeat remain healthy. Setup/starter remain failed and scientific environment capability is unavailable; the original audit revision remains. Independent system Python still executes. This does **not** establish safe prefix rollback.
- Restoring the test channel and retrying via product `POST /environment-setup` recovers without restarting the Runner; a new revision is recorded and utilities/Python execute successfully.
- A separate Bash stdin probe locates NUL removal in Bash script parsing. Bash-to-batch invocation expands `%PATH%`; this is distinct from the service helper's verified literal preservation. No global rejection rule was added.

Product acceptance ran on the uncommitted candidate based on `b9cb7c02250815f6aad729c2ee647c80bfec6e77`; the submitted product source is unchanged. The focused 8-test and 13-test commands were rerun after committing. Remote Runners, sandbox modes, browser UI journeys, and external live models were not covered. Test services were stopped after evidence capture.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix`

User impact: the model receives actionable command-not-found recovery advice and a precise explanation of Python independence when managed Bash is unavailable.

Compatibility and migration: none.

fix(kubernetes): reload workloads on environment secret change

Closes #254

mountConfiguration returned early when the component had no config
file, so the Reloader annotation was never set, even when the
environment secret came from an external secret. Rotating that secret
did not restart the pods. The annotation now lists the environment
secret and the config secret whenever they exist, and the redundant
config check is gone. A web-service fixture with only an environment
secret covers the case in the snapshot.

benchmarks.task_description:
fix(kubernetes): run bun() with bun and fix package entry points

Closes #255

The bun() command helper was a copy of node() and returned the Node
binary. It now returns /usr/local/bin/bun, the path where the root
dockerfile installs Bun in the runner image. package.json pointed main
and types to a missing main.ts instead of src/main.ts, and the
import-api-resources script called pnpm although the repository uses
Bun.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

benchmarks.task_description:
fix(kubernetes): read every external secret from the scaleway store

Closes #252

The shared store constant targeted the gcp cluster secret store while
WorkloadEnvironment and ImageRegistryAuth hard-coded scaleway, so a
workload read its config secret and its environment secret from
different stores. Point the constant to scaleway and use it everywhere.

ExternalSecretRef also ignored options.version and always wrote
latest. Honor it (latest stays the default) and let
ExternalSecret.ref() pass it through.

The constant is renamed SCALEWAY_SECRET_STORE, after the store it targets.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

benchmarks.task_description:
fix(kubernetes): make ingress annotations optional and use nginx keys

Closes #253

IngressConfig.annotations required all three fields while WebService
already reads each one with a default, so setting one annotation forced
the caller to set them all. The SSL redirect used the generic
ingress.kubernetes.io prefix, which ingress-nginx ignores; the proxy
body size already targets ingress-nginx, so both now use the
nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io prefix.

No chart exposes an ingress yet, so a test-only fixture snapshots a
WebService with an ingress to lock the generated YAML.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

fix(kubernetes): point workloads to the mounted config file

Closes #251

The workloads mount config.json in /app/config but set neither
CONFIG_FILE_PATH nor NODE_ENV, so the account app falls back to
config.test.json and starts on the schema defaults.

When a config.json is mounted, the container now gets
CONFIG_FILE_PATH=/app/config/config.json and NODE_ENV=production.
Values declared in the workload environment take precedence over
these defaults, so an explicit value is never replaced.

fix(kubernetes): synthesize the scopes stored in maps

Closes #247

The application and environment scopes are stored in `Map` instances, but `synthesizeAllResources` iterated them with `Object.values()`, which returns an empty array for a `Map`. No scope was synthesized and no manifest was written.

Iterating with `.values()` fixes it: `bun src/main.ts` now writes `manifests/account-service/development.yaml`.

No changeset: the `kubernetes` workspace is ignored by Changesets.

Keep console scroll position and focus when a console setting changes

## References

Fixes #20363.

## Code changes

Any change to the Code Console settings called `CodeConsole.setConfig` on every open console, and `setConfig` always ended with `_updateLayout`, which detaches and re-inserts the input and output panes, resets their sizes, scrolls the output to the top and focuses the prompt. The toolbar factory also cleared and refilled every toolbar on any settings change, even when the toolbar definition itself was unchanged.

`CodeConsole.setConfig` now only calls `_updateLayout` when `promptCellPosition` actually changed, or when the panes were never laid out. The other settings are read when cells execute or banners are created, so they do not need a layout rebuild. `_updateLayout` now only re-focuses the prompt when focus was already inside that console, instead of stealing focus from another console or the settings editor. The toolbar factory's `transferSettings` returns early when the toolbar definition is unchanged, so identical items are no longer cleared and re-added (which rebuilt every toolbar and could reorder its items).

## User-facing changes

Changing a console setting that does not change the layout (for example Settings > Auto Close Brackets) no longer scrolls every open console to the top, no longer moves focus to another console, and no longer reorders toolbar items.

## Backwards-incompatible changes

None.
